messages:
Maya: Quick kickoff - I put together a proposal for a multi-quarter plan on geo-slices + routing policies. Goal: give sales a predictable path for regional guarantees while keeping hosted cost-efficiency. doc: https://intra.redwood/geo-slices (TL;DR in thread).
Rafi: skimmed. main question: do we prioritize strict egress controls first or affinity+cache improvements? Customers ask both.
Lena: my vote = affinity+cache first. cheaper and reduces token-cost variance for customers that just want lower latency. egress/compliance is a bigger legal lift.
Chris: agree with Lena. also important: define a default fallback lane so apps don't see timeouts during regional saturation.
Priya: sales asked for a simple SLA badge they can promise: "90ms p95 within region" - is that realistic with soft-slices only?
Maya: probably not immediately. Proposed phases: 
Phase A - Policy & Observability: routing DSL, per-request region hinting, metrics (p50/p95/p99 by region), and rollout tooling.
Phase B - Affinity + Cache Slices: logical slices with sticky routing and prefix/KV cache partitioning (no dedicated GPUs).
Phase C - Reserved Pools: routable capacity pools customers can reserve (Reserved/Dedicated).
Phase D - Private Deployments & Egress Enforcement: full network/KMS controls for compliance customers.
Rafi: gating ideas by phase: A = 100% telemetry + real-time policy eval; B = canary traffic with eviction metrics + cold-miss under 95th percentile; C = billing & quota plumbing + capacity isolation test; D = legal signoff + audit logs.
Lena: small config example for the routing DSL we sketched earlier: 
```
when: request.region == customer.region
then: route(prefer_local, fallback: reserved_pool, global)
```
Chris: ops note: eviction policy needs a safe default. If we evict aggressively, tail latency spikes. propose evict_after = 10m by default with hysteresis.
Priya: customers for pilot: NeonApps (high latency sensitivity), MediPay (compliance), and Shoply (cost-sensitive). I'll coordinate.
Maya: tentative timeline suggestion: Phase A in 6 weeks; Phase B in next quarter; Phase C following quarter; Phase D next following quarter. dependent on infra spike results.
Rafi: engineering sizing rough: A = 3 SWE + 1 infra (3w), B = 6 SWE + infra changes (8w), C = 5 SWE + networking (6w), D = 4 SWE + security/compliance (6w).
Priya: ask to include cost-delta per-phase for renewals team. they want to know seat vs usage lift.
Lena: will run a micro-benchmark for prefix caching memory growth and post numbers in the doc by EOD Tue.
infra-bot: Scheduled deployment window: infra-spike/geo-cache-eval on 2025-09-03 :calendar:
Chris: I'll draft the fallback playbook: how to detect regional overload and route to fallback without broken sessions. aim to have a first pass by Friday.
Maya: decisions for track: (1) start with affinity+cache not egress, (2) pilot NeonApps in Phase B, (3) require telemetry coverage before any canary. I'll update roadmap board.
Rafi: one more - define UX for callers: should API support explicit region param or only hints? I prefer hints to keep control.
Priya: sales prefers an explicit opt-in flag for reserved pools so they can sell it clearly.
Maya: ok action items:
- Lena: micro-bench on cache memory impact (deliver Tue)
- Chris: fallback runbook draft (Fri)
- Priya: lock pilots and capture acceptance criteria (Mon)
- Rafi: write short doc on routing DSL semantics + example policies (end of week)
Maya: thanks all. If no objections I'll spin this into a roadmap card and assign owners. :white_check_mark:
Lena: no objections.
Priya: good to go.
Chris: 👍
Maya: closing thread.
